correctness.rationale: Every conic bundle has at least one singular fiber because X has Euler number 12 but a smooth P1-bundle has 4. Costa Theorem 4.2 forces a singular fiber to equal two sections meeting once. With no reducible elliptic fibers, the MW group equals E8, and sections indexed by v,w meet in ||v-w||^2/2-1 points. Translating one section to zero reduces to O+S_u with ||u||^2=4. These divisors are nef, isotropic and have elliptic-fiber degree 2, hence Costa Theorem 3.8 makes conic pencils. Two such pencils are translation equivalent iff u-u’ is in 2E8, by E8 projections and the square-zero/fiber-degree equations. The standalone deterministic exact checker exhaustively enumerates all 2160 norm-4 E8 vectors and their 135 classes of 16; an independent root-basis count gives 136 mod-two isotropic classes with zero unrepresented. The eight A2 singular fibers follow from Euler number 12=4+8.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Costa establishes that every conic pencil contains reducible A2 fibers when no elliptic fibers are reducible; Schütt–Shioda identifies the MW lattice with E8. The numerical count of translation orbits requires a further equivalence proof for norm-four section differences modulo 2E8 and an exact full E8 residue-class census. The eight-fiber fact is a known-type consequence of Euler characteristic, not claimed as an independent general theorem. Existing source frameworks are credited as indispensable ingredients.

originality.rationale: The source literature supplies conic class and singular fiber classifications and the E8 Mordell–Weil lattice, but the inspected relevant full-text sections do not enumerate Mordell–Weil translation orbits. The new classification identifies the exact quotient by 2E8 and counts its 135 geometric orbits using a complete finite norm-four computation. A new, nontrivial quotient classification is not the same statement as the unrestricted conic-class correspondence. The literature overlap risk is disclosed.

value.rationale: Counting geometric conic fibrations up to their natural infinite Mordell–Weil symmetry is a motivated complete orbit classification on an important non-Mori-dream rational elliptic surface. The exact finite answer 135 and its E8/2E8 quadratic-form labeling connect the geometry of conic bundles to the finite orthogonal geometry of E8 and explain the systematic eight reducible fibers. This is not an arbitrary finite parameter slice, nor merely rebranding the numerical conic-class criterion.
